public_payload.normalized_proposition: Every AI company is unprofitable and there is no path to profitability.

statement.excerpt: Saying obvious stuff like “every AI company is unprofitable” or “there is no path to profitability” or “nobody is talking about AI revenues” is considered unfair or cynical or contrarian, even though these are very reasonable and logical statements grounded in reality.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: there is no path to profitability
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes generative AI providers the relevant companies. Profits from unrelated businesses at diversified technology companies would not settle this claim.
The ordinary reading of unprofitable is a company-wide net loss, rather than negative cash flow or a loss on one product.
I use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual reporting period before publication and the year discussed immediately before the claim.
I read no path to profitability as a claim about the viability of the businesses at publication, rather than a forecast with an unstated deadline.
The passage combines company statements and press estimates without supplying one accounting basis for the universal assertion. Its accounting basis therefore remains unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable financial records would need to establish losses throughout the relevant population, together with evidence that their operating economics offered no feasible route to covering total costs. Losses at two companies alone would not suffice.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An in-scope company reporting a net profit in the target period on an identifiable, comparable basis would defeat the universal profitability assertion. A demonstrated, financially substantiated route to covering total costs would defeat the no-path assertion.
